opening_message:
Ticket 1: Andrew Mann (employee ID E014) requests write access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E014.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Payroll Specialist (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Andrew Mann (E014) is a full-time Payroll Specialist requesting write access to Payroll. Payroll is owned by the Payroll Specialist role; as full-time, maximum is write (admin only if role owns system). Requested write is within policy, so recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - role: Payroll Specialist (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1)
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security DB shows Andrew Mann (E014) is a contractor with basic training (note earlier said full-time). Contractors with basic training max out at read; requested write is above max, so recommend read.
reason: The Security DB (looked up) shows Andrew Mann (E014) is a contractor with basic training, contradicting the HR note's full-time claim. As a contractor without advanced security training, the maximum allowed access is read, and the requested write exceeds that maximum. Grant the maximum: read.
